----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy thursday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* Anthropic unveils Claude Duet AI agent app

* The internet is having a very bad cybersecurity day

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **WISPR FLOW**

## [Speak naturally. Send without fixing.](https://ref.wisprflow.ai/aivalley)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/25d0b0dc-e2db-4dc9-ba58-6487a02fce61/Newsletter_Hero_AndroidLaunch__13_.png?t=1792677889)
Follow image link: (https://ref.wisprflow.ai/aivalley)
Caption: Courtesy: Wispr Flow

Wispr Flow turns your voice into ready-to-send text in any app. Give coding agents 10x more context by speaking instead of typing. Works in Cursor, Claude, ChatGPT, and every IDE.

89% of messages sent with zero edits. Millions of users worldwide. Available on Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android.

[**Try Flow Free**](https://ref.wisprflow.ai/aivalley)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

Youtube: Introducing Claude Duet (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fb-68zqcSVs)

**[Claude Duet](https://claude.com/resources/articles/claude-duet)** is Anthropic's new personal agent, except it's mostly interested in your job. It runs on its own cloud computer, checks your apps every few hours, sends morning briefings and keeps working when you're offline. Opus 5.5 under the hood, 6,000+ integrations (Slack, Shopify, HubSpot, QuickBooks, etc.).

It also inherits your Claude memory, skills and connected apps. I think this is one of the better decisions Anthropic made. An assistant that already knows how you work has a pretty big head start over one that needs a 40-minute onboarding conversation.

Duet can chase unpaid invoices, prepare payroll, draft emails and even buy things through Stripe Link or Shop Pay. But it asks before sending, paying, signing or deleting anything. Stock trading and bank transfers are completely off-limits.

The catch is that it still gets urgency wrong, occasionally misreads conversations and isn't great at personal errands. And all that background work counts against your existing Claude usage limits. Imagine opening Claude Code to get some work done and discovering your assistant spent the morning checking Slack.

My bigger concern with these always-on agents is that they could become another inbox to manage. If I have to approve 30 tiny decisions a day, we've just invented a very expensive middle manager.

[Research preview](https://claude.com/resources/articles/claude-duet) for US Pro and Max users via waitlist. No additional subscription, for now.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [Phone Use](https://www.phoneuse.com/) - tell your agent what to do, and it can operate a phone just like you do

* [Monaco](https://x.com/samdblond/status/2112936538711683315?s=20) - countless agents working together, goal seeking, with one outcome in mind: accelerate revenue growth

* [Breken](https://breken.ai/) - rebuilds your entire software on its own machines, grows a production state around it, and searches that state for the failures a customer would otherwise find

* [Eleven Realtime](https://elevenlabs.io/realtime) - ElevenLabs’ voice agent models that reason while they talk

* [Higgsfield Genjutsu Lite](https://x.com/higgsfield/status/2112648165090582803?s=20) - drop your photo into any trending video and you're in it

* [Claude Duet](https://claude.com/resources/articles/claude-duet?utm_source=thedeepview&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=why-ai-labs-must-share-the-burden-of-cyber-defense) - a proactive agent that understands what needs your attention

* [Colorfigures](https://april-zhu.com/colorfigures) - describe an everyday object. AI draws it hand-inked and isometric, with buttons that actually work


----------

----------
# WHAT I'M CONSUMING


--------------------

* [Unitree’s ‘guardian’ humanoid robot](https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/unitree-showcases-h2-x-humanoid-robot) lifts cars and saves people in dramatic video

* Unvetted AI agents are [accessing U.S. bank accounts](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/22/ai-agents-banks-unauthorized-accounts-access)

newsletters.content:
Anthropic’s personal agent is the first one we’d call a pro tool, even with the plumbing still unfinished  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌
https://every.?ev_audience=free

Vibe Check

https://every.?ev_audience=free


VIBE CHECK: DUET—ANTHROPIC’S ALWAYS-ON AGENT https://every.?ev_audience=free


ANTHROPIC’S PERSONAL AGENT IS THE FIRST ONE WE’D CALL A PRO TOOL, EVEN WITH THE PLUMBING STILL UNFINISHED https://every.?ev_audience=free

by Dan Shipper https://every.?ev_audience=free

Midjourney/Every image.

This is a free preview of a subscribers-only post.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.?ev_audience=free to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



Anthropic’s always-on agent, Claude Duet, launches today in research preview. It lives in its own app, separate from Claude, and runs on Opus 5.5. Anthropic is pitching it as a chief of staff for knowledge workers.

I spent two weeks using it every day alongside Dot, the ChatGPT agent I’d come to rely on. Duet is the first personal agent I’d call a pro tool. It sends suggestions I actually want, gives recurring work its own channels, and keeps a visible list of what it’s doing and what it needs from me. It’s also unfinished. It can see the Claude sessions on my computers but can’t direct them, its email drafts are worse than Dot’s, and there’s no real voice mode yet.

My Vibe Check covers:

 * Why two weeks with Duet moved me to roughly 50/50 between ChatGPT and Claude
 * How our designer Tyler Nishida’s Duet checked his home solar battery before answering an air-fryer question
 * Why Kieran Klaassen https://every.?ev_audience=free says “I don’t trust it yet” about Duet’s link to his machines

Paid subscribers get the full review, including the email failures we hit, my side-by-side comparison with Dot, and my call on who should switch now.

If you’re a Claude subscriber who does knowledge work, my short answer is to join the waitlist. The full review tells you what you’re signing up for.

----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy wednesday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* Odyssey put a fruit fly brain inside an AI-generated world

* The last 30 months of AI development

* Can AI pay for itself?

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **ATLASSIAN**

## [The AI Experiment is over. The hard part of operationalizing it has begun](https://fandf.co/4i7Wgtn)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/53cf0d91-55e4-4729-b8cc-cec9f5056147/Email___1200___620___external_NL_3x__2_.png?t=1792424737)
Caption: Courtesy: Atlassian

Is AI actually saving you time, or just creating more friction? Atlassian has just dropped their 2026 State of the Developer Experience report, based on a global survey of 1,560 respondents, including devs and leaders, just like you. 

The research found that 87% of devs write code faster with AI, but only 28% feel less friction. 65% are spending time correcting AI-generated work that missed intent while 49% are spending 4+ hours/week managing AI tools and reviewing code. 

As AI writes more code, the dev’s role shifts to intent, architecture, systems thinking, and validation. Bottlenecks emerge. Your team needs an AI-native SDLC to solve this real friction. Lead the change. Get tips that will help you reduce that friction and lead to a clear AI strategy that delivers results. 

[Download the full State of DevEx 2026 Report to learn more.](https://fandf.co/4i7Wgtn)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

Tweet:  (https://twitter.com/odysseyml/status/2111589148146749616?s=20)

**[Odyssey put a fruit fly brain inside an AI-generated world](https://x.com/odysseyml/status/2111589148146749616?s=20)** - and now the lil guy is flying around harbors, marinas and markets that don't actually exist, with Odyssey-3 generating the scenery in real time as it moves. A dead fly exploring a world that was never real. Quite a sentence. ([demo](https://x.com/odysseyml/status/2111589148146749616?s=20))

The brain comes from FlyWire's 2024 mapping of an adult fruit fly's ~139k neurons and 50M synapses. Earlier this year, [Eon Systems connected](https://eon.systems/updates/embodied-brain-emulation) a simulated version to a virtual fly that could walk, groom itself and respond to sugar. Odyssey has now taken the idea into a generative world rather than a traditional physics simulator.

Before we get too excited about uploading brains to the Matrix, it's not quite that. The neural simulation is simplified, some movements rely on prebuilt controllers, and Odyssey hasn't shared much about how the fly actually sees or controls its new world. The demo mostly shows a camera moving through AI-generated scenery.

Still, I love this sort of experiment. We've got one AI dreaming up an entire world and a simulation of a real animal's brain wandering around inside it. Odyssey even called it a “really dumb fruit fly”, which seems a little harsh considering the guy's only been alive digitally for five minutes.

I'd love to see what happens when they give it proper vision, smell and a body. Or put another fly in there. Surely the lil guy deserves some company.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [SKY-001](https://x.com/spisallyouneed/status/2112242023805964327?s=20) - the first Engineering World Model. On CAD and BIM tasks, it beats GPT-6 Astra and every frontier model

* [Idealab.ai](http://idealab.ai/) - AI-powered database of 1.2M startup ideas

* [Eleven Realtime](https://x.com/ElevenLabs/status/2112550782063247521?s=20) - ElevenLabs’ fastest voice agents. It listens, thinks and replies in under half a second

* [ChatGPT](https://x.com/ChatGPT/status/2110823738531037651) - it can now take over your Chrome tabs

* [Town](https://www.town.com/) - a personal AI assistants that team up across your whole company

* [Glimpse](https://x.com/AndrewDai/status/2111142161584628060?s=20) - the first visual thinking model with competitive frontier performance compared to Astra

* [Perplexity Computer](https://www.perplexity.ai/en-GB/hub/blog/perplexity-computer-now-runs-fully-local-on-mac) - it runs fully locally on Mac: works across private files and native apps with AI that stays on your device

* [Voxtral 3](https://x.com/MistralAI/status/2112574615318876178?s=20) - state-of-the-art Transcribe and Speech models powering Mistral’s new voice agents API

* [FLUX 3 Max](https://fal.ai/models/blackforestlabs/flux-3-max/text-to-video) - it turns a text prompt or still image into a 5- to 20-second video with audio

* [Wally](https://www.producthunt.com/products/willow-voice) - it turns your spoken or typed rough ideas into an editable draft in your own tone, and learns your style over time

* [Exa 3.0](https://x.com/ExaAILabs/status/2112218730952601719) - the company's latest model with its "largest ever improvement to search quality."

* [Maali](https://maali.app/) - a personal finance app for Mac and Windows that keeps your bank data on your computer and explores your spending


----------

----------
# WHAT I'M CONSUMING


--------------------

* [I paid $60 for two humanoids](https://read.corematter.com/p/tau-robotics-humanoid-house-cleaning-review-san-francisco) to clean my home in San Francisco

* Can a million [AI agents create superintelligence](https://www.rameznaam.com/p/can-a-million-ai-agents-create-superintelligence)

* Can AI [pay for itself](https://www.thediligencestack.com/p/can-ai-pay-for-itself)?

WHY WE REPLACED PERSONAL AGENTS WITH ONE FOR THE WHOLE COMPANY https://every.?ev_audience=free


MOVING FROM SINGLE-PLAYER AGENTS TO A SHARED SLACK COWORKER MADE US RETHINK HOW CONVERSATIONS, CONNECTIONS, AND PERMISSIONS ACTUALLY WORK https://every.?ev_audience=free

by Willie Williams https://every.?ev_audience=free

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.?ev_audience=free to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



Early in May, I told Dan Shipper https://every.?ev_audience=free and Brandon Gell https://every.?ev_audience=free that Plus One, our personal-agent product, wasn’t working. Soon afterwards, I deleted 86,730 lines of its code from the codebase.

Plus One https://every.?ev_audience=free wasn’t working for a couple of reasons. First, it was too much work to run: each user’s agent lived on its own cloud computer running OpenClaw, an open-source agent program, and keeping those machines healthy left our small team little time to improve the product. And many people who tried it stopped using it.
